newsitem.title: USA: Orange County assistant treasurer trial begins.
newsitem.headline: Orange County assistant treasurer trial begins.

text.p: The criminal trial of former Orange County assistant treasurer Matthew Raabe got under way on Wednesday, more than two years after the county's staggering investment losses forced it into bankruptcy.

Jury selection began Wednesday morning in a Santa Ana courtroom and was expected to last for several days. Hundreds of potential jurors were being considered for the panel. Attorneys planned to begin questioning them early next week.
"We anticipate that there will be people with opinions, and that's why we have so many (potential) jurors," Raabe's attorney, Gary Pohlson, told Reuters.
Raabe's attorney said he was "very optimistic" that the trial would vindicate his client, who has denied any wrongdoing. Raabe faces up to 12 years in state prison.
Testimony in the trial was expected to begin March 24. The trial was expected to last through late April or early May, Deputy Orange County District Attorney Matthew Anderson said.
The county filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
From March 1993 until he was placed on administrative leave in January 1995, Raabe was the assistant treasurer of the county. The county fired him that March.
Raabe was indicted in May 1995 on several felony counts, including making false statements in the sale of securities and misappropriation of public funds.
Raabe was one of several local officials to face charges following the bankruptcy.
In April 1995, former county treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work programme instead of jail.
Citron's attorney claimed that his client was "manipulated" by Raabe, who he said was the "mastermind."
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
The case against county auditor Steven Lewis has been put on hold by a state court pending a decision on his motion to disqualify the district attorney.
